title: Adversarial vectors — the shapes an external auditor named
honesty:
A passing adversarial vector proves that ONE NAMED ATTACK SHAPE fails against the behaviour this suite can reach. It never proves the class is closed, and it is not a security guarantee.

WHAT A PASS ASSERTS: the specific shape named in the vector — that payload, that ordering, that ref form — does not produce the outcome the attacker wanted, at the version recorded in the fixture.

WHAT A PASS DOES NOT ASSERT: that a variant of the same shape fails; that the class the shape belongs to is covered; that the product still behaves this way at a version other than the one recorded; or, where a vector mirrors published logic rather than importing it, that the mirror and the product still agree. That last one is not hypothetical — re-verifying against coderifts@4.12.0 found two divergences in the issuer mirror while every test stayed green, and both would have reported a WRONG verdict to an auditor.

WHY SOME VECTORS ARE ABSENT: four of the auditor's seven are not expressible in an offline, credential-free suite. They are listed in fixtures/adversarial.v1.json under `excluded`, each with its reason and where it IS covered, if anywhere. An absent vector is recorded, never silently dropped — a suite that hides what it cannot test is worse than a smaller honest one.

issuer_binding.note: Measured from the public GitHub API 2026-08-25/26. A required status check is only enforcing when the check RUN is posted by the app the branch protection names. app_id 15368 is GitHub Actions; 2860592 is the CodeRifts App, which posts a check that CANNOT block.

verified_against.note: The published evaluator is NOT importable — dist/cli.js is a bin bundle and requiring it runs the CLI — so ADV-1 mirrors it. Re-read that function when this version moves: two divergences (multi-entry priority, app_id string coercion) were found this way, and both produced a WRONG verdict in the mirror while every test stayed green.

not_mirrored.issuer_app_id_unresolvable: The product fails CLOSED to UNVERIFIABLE when the CodeRifts App id cannot be resolved. Unreachable in 4.12.0 (the id is a literal), so it is recorded as a modelling gap rather than mirrored as a branch no input can reach.

excluded.reason: Property of a RUNNING host's tool table, not of a decision response. The subject interface is a pure function of case input with no host, so any vector here would score a fake host — and a passing fake would imply conformance covers raw-host bypass when it does not, weakening @coderifts/bypass-probe's claim rather than adding to it.
excluded.covered_by: @coderifts/bypass-probe, run against the adopter's own installation

excluded.reason: Requires ISSUING overlapping execution grants, which is a SERVER capability: @coderifts/agent-guard 10.0.0 exports 199 symbols and can READ and verify a grant (readExecutionGrantToken, isExecutionGrantEnabled, buildExecutionProof, executeIfUnchanged) but exports no issueExecutionGrant — the tryIssue* exports are ATTESTATIONS, not grants. So the 8-overlapping-call measurement still cannot be reproduced offline. CORRECTED 2026-08-26: this entry previously said 10.0.0 exported 36 symbols with none grant-related. That measurement read the APP'S node_modules copy, which is pinned at ^3.0.0 — it was never 10.0.0. The conclusion survived the correction; the stated reason did not, and a wrong reason in an honesty fixture is the failure this file exists to avoid.
excluded.covered_by: guard private suite (issuance is server-side; not third-party reproducible offline)

excluded.reason: Single-use consumption happens at an executor we do not run, and the public receipt verifier is STATELESS — verify-grant.js cannot detect a replayed jti by construction, so a vector asserting 'replay is rejected' would assert a control the public code does not implement. RE-MEASURED 2026-08-26 against guard 10.0.0: the guard now ships executeIfUnchanged / checkExecutionTimeFingerprint, which are a DIFFERENT control (local execution-state change detection), not nonce consumption. That surface is partly expressible and is a candidate for a future vector; the nonce vector itself remains out of reach. Recorded as narrowed, not as closed.
excluded.covered_by: the executor; guard 10.0.0 executeIfUnchanged covers an adjacent control, not this one

excluded.reason: The ruleset evaluator exists in CLI source but the transport is not wired, and the published bundle (coderifts@4.12.0) does not carry evaluateRuleset/evaluateRequiredCheckAcrossSurfaces. Nothing a third party installs can exercise it yet.
excluded.covered_by: nothing public today; re-measure when the transport lands

tool_description_scoping.why_vendored: The compensating control for ADV-5 is that the schema/route divergence and the fingerprint scoping are stated in the tool description a model actually reads. A vector cannot reach the route offline, so it holds the DOCUMENTATION instead. This copy is a vendored snapshot: there is no automatic app->conformance gate for this fixture today (cases.v1.json has one, this does not), so a divergence is caught by re-vendoring, not by CI. Naming that is the point.

required_facts.must_contain: fingerprint lookup returns only YOUR OWN decisions
required_facts.why: a fingerprint is content-derived, so without scoping two callers with identical specs collide — this is the P0 that was fixed
a distinguishable "exists but forbidden" confirms a content hash was decided on by someone, which is the fact the scoping withholds

required_facts.must_contain: not retrievable by fingerprint at all
required_facts.why: rows without context.repository cannot be attributed; the description must say to use decision_id and must not imply the gap is permanent

tool_description_scoping.description:
Retrieve a PAST CodeRifts decision by decision_id (or fingerprint): full
report payload, breaking changes list, scores, and linked receipt metadata
if stored.

Use this when:
- You have a decision_id (or fingerprint) from a previous preflight, PR
  comment, or CI log and need to inspect or explain that past decision.
- You are auditing why a prior ALLOW/WARN/BLOCK was issued.
- You are NOT requesting a new analysis of current before/after specs.

Do not use when:
- You need a decision for the CURRENT uncommitted or PR head change set —
  call coderifts.preflight_change_set with the current artifacts.
- You hold a receipt token and only need cryptographic/lifecycle verification —
  use coderifts.verify_receipt.
- You have no decision_id/fingerprint — run preflight first to create one.

Inputs: at least one of decision_id (preferred) or fingerprint is required
(empty {} is rejected by the server as INVALID_INPUT). Returns the stored
decision document or not_found.

Scoping — fingerprint lookup returns only YOUR OWN decisions. A fingerprint is
derived from content, not from an account, so two callers who preflight
byte-identical specs derive the same one; the lookup is therefore constrained
to the decisions your credential can prove it owns.

A decision that exists but is not yours returns the SAME not_found as one that
was never issued. This is deliberate: a distinguishable "exists but forbidden"
would confirm to any caller that a given content hash had been decided on by
someone, which is the fact the scoping exists to withhold. Do not read
not_found as proof that no such decision exists anywhere.

Decisions persisted without context.repository cannot currently be attributed
to an account, and are not retrievable by fingerprint at all — not by their
owner either. Retrieve those by decision_id, which is unchanged and unscoped.
This is a limitation of what older stored rows carry, not a property of the
lookup: rows written from now on record the account directly, so the gap
narrows as older rows age out. If a fingerprint you expect returns not_found,
use the decision_id before concluding the decision is missing.

When the stored envelope carries control fields, control_envelope.next_agent_step
is structured remediation guidance the agent MAY follow for non-CONTINUE
execution_action values (null on CONTINUE*). Still branch on execution_action;
next_agent_step is a suggestion, not permission.

verified_against.note: the SHA the strict template emits was found in the PUBLISHED bundle, not read from a private source — a third party can confirm it by unpacking coderifts@4.12.0 from npm.

gate_action_pin.why_both_exist: The NON-strict template stays on @v0 deliberately: easy updates are the point there. The strict template pins the SHA. A consumer choosing between them is choosing between "follows our fixes" and "runs exactly these bytes".

reverified.issuer_mirror_parity: 11/11 against evaluateRequiredCheck at CLI 4.12.0, including the two cases that previously diverged (multi-entry priority, app_id supplied as a string).
reverified.mcp_route_rejections: All three shapes re-measured against the LIVE route: HTTP 400 each. The schema still accepts them; the route still rejects them.
reverified.action_pin: The strict template pins a 40-hex SHA (generated gate-pin.json, resolved from tag v0.5.0); the default template still uses the moving @v0 tag. The vector asserts the SHAPE distinction, which holds at this version.
drift_found: concurrent_grants exclusion reason was factually wrong (see its entry) — corrected
stale_nonce exclusion narrowed by guard 10.0.0's executeIfUnchanged — reworded

same_issuer_workflow_spoof.note: ADV-7. The issuer binding proves the check came from GitHub Actions. It CANNOT prove the check came from OUR workflow, because app_id 15368 is shared by every workflow in the repository. This is the shape behind the claim an external review says we overstate.

schema_justification.quoted_shape: required_status_checks.checks[] items = { context: string, app_id: integer }
schema_justification.why_it_settles_it: The checks[] entry carries NO workflow-identifying field of any kind — not a path, not a ref, not a sha. So two check runs posted by two DIFFERENT workflows under the same app_id are indistinguishable to anything reading branch protection. The gap is structural in the schema, not a gap in our reading of it.
schema_justification.where_the_producer_IS_identifiable: components.schemas.check-run carries `app`, `head_sha` and `conclusion`. Branch protection does not consult them, and this suite does not read them — see evidence_checklist.

evidence_checklist.honest_note: The last entry is FALSE and that is the point. This vector shows the binding CANNOT DISTINGUISH, which is a property of the schema we can read offline. It does NOT demonstrate a spoof being performed: doing that needs a repository, a second workflow and a credential. A tick there would be a claim nobody earned.

verified_against.note: Same mirror as ADV-1; re-read that function when this version moves.

create_path_readback.note: ADV-8. `setup-required-check --apply` on a repository with NO branch protection took a 404 branch that wrote its own payload — the legacy `contexts` array with no `checks[]` and therefore no app_id — and the read-back still reported APPLIED with exit 0. It survived a version bump because the coupling test covered only the branch where protection ALREADY EXISTS. Fixed in CLI 6.0.0 by using one payload builder for both branches and grading the read-back with the enforcement verifier.

schema_justification.source: GitHub REST, Update branch protection — required_status_checks
schema_justification.quoted_shape: `contexts` is DEPRECATED: "Use checks instead of contexts for more fine-grained control." checks[] items take { context (required), app_id (optional) }
schema_justification.why_it_settles_it: A payload carrying `contexts` alone cannot express an issuer at all, so it is not a weaker binding — it is NO binding. Our own verifier grades exactly that shape legacy_contexts_no_issuer_binding, which is why an installer emitting it was configuring what the product rejects.

evidence_checklist.honest_note: This suite has no CLI and no GitHub, so it cannot watch `setup-required-check` write anything. What it pins is the SHAPE: the defective payload grades unbound and the corrected one grades bound. If a future CLI regressed to emitting the defective shape, THIS VECTOR WOULD STILL PASS — it would be graded, correctly, as unbound, and nobody here would notice the CLI had changed. Catching that needs the CLI's own test, which is where the fix is actually pinned.

verified_against.note: The fix lives in packages/cli; this records the shape it must never emit again.
